translation_notes: prefixes: dc, dcterms, prof, rdfs, sdo, skos. The draft also declared owl and rdf, which the region never uses: removed (the new triple `{o} a prof:ResourceDescriptor` uses `a`).

All reads are translated: each `self.G.subject_objects(P)` is `m{ ?s P ?o }` inside the original `chain(...)`. The stratum sites, 14 `self.G.remove((s, P, o))` over five loops, are all fully bound: `-{ {s} P {o} }`, one island per removal. A `;` fold would be a DELETE WHERE join that removes nothing when one of the three or four triples is absent (the fixture has such subjects, e.g. one with only dc:title).

The removals happen while the chain is still being walked (a value carried by dc:title, skos:prefLabel and dcterms:title on one subject is removed at the first source, so the later generators no longer yield it). m{ } is lazy like the rdflib generator, and the fixture has that subject (ex:l4, ex:c5): same graph on both sides.
`@graph self.G` designates an attribute and adds the six prefixes to the caller's graph without overwriting its bindings; the harness compares bindings and is green.
Context shim pylode_context.py: Prof reduced to its `G` attribute (the real __init__ parses a profile). pyLODE 2.13.2 is not importable here (installed pylode is 3.2.3, a different API).

Driver: whole fixture, a graph with nothing to expand, the fixture with dc:title already moved. Mutants killed: `-{ {s} skos:prefLabel ?x }`, `-{ {s} ?p {o} }` (neighbours sharing subject and value under another predicate), `m{ ?s prof:hasResource ?o }` pointed at prof:isProfileOf. Equivalent mutant, noted: `-{ ?x sdo:description {o} }` (every such triple is itself in the loop's source set).
optimization_notes: optimized.py: the five copy-and-remove loops become one loop over a table (target, sources); for each source, `self.G.subject_objects(source)` walks lazily as the chain did (so a value removed at an earlier source is not yielded again), the removals become `self.G -= [(s, p, o) for p in sources]` and the add stays. The Resource Descriptors loop reads `self.G.objects(None, PROF.hasResource)`; `itertools.chain` is no longer used. The section headings '# label', '# comment', '# creator', '# contributor', '# publisher' labelled the merged loops and go; '# Agents', the conflation comment and '# Resource Descriptors' stay.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the same table with prefixed names, `m{ ?s {source} ?o }` with the predicate interpolated, `+{ {s} {target} {o} }` under `@graph self.G`, and `m{ [] prof:hasResource ?o }` for the last loop.

Exception to line-for-line identity, not to the symmetry: the removal is `for p in sources:` + `-{ {s} {p} {o} }` in optimized.ldpy (4 tokens fewer than the `-=` comprehension there), while optimized.py keeps `self.G -= [...]`, its own shortest form; the loop is longer in Python, so nothing is carried back.
